blocks.text:
We have reached the leaf.
Now we need to go inside.

Inside a cell.
Then inside a chloroplast.
A small structure where photosynthesis happens.

Here, membranes hold molecules of chlorophyll.
These molecules can absorb light.

I know the word.
But “absorbing light” is still hard for me to picture.

The chlorophyll molecule already contains electrons.
When it absorbs our photon, it enters a higher-energy electronic state.
We call this an excited state.

The photon has not become an electron.
It has transferred its energy.

And at this first moment, the electron is still part of the molecule.
It has not been passed to another molecule yet.

The photon’s journey ends here.
But the energy’s journey continues.

No sugar has been made yet.
The first change is much smaller.
A molecule now has energy it did not have before.
What can the plant do with it?

notes.title: Inside the leaf
paragraphs: A chloroplast is a structure inside a plant cell. Its thylakoid membranes contain light-harvesting complexes: proteins holding chlorophyll and other pigments.

notes.title: Absorption is not electron transfer
paragraphs: Absorption creates electronic excitation. It does not mean that an electron has already been passed to another molecule. Excitation energy can move later through the pigment network.

notes.title: Where this draft stops
paragraphs: This passage covers arrival, chlorophyll and absorption only. Reaction centres, water, ATP, NADPH and carbon fixation come later.
